exposure: perinatal tissue type (amniotic fluid, amniotic membrane, umbilical cord, intact placenta, placental fragments)
delivery mode (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
collection timing (within vs. outside laboratory working hours)
outcome: processing feasibility (material acquisition difficulty, transportation logistics, storage duration, processing complexity)
cohort: The study included 32 healthy term pregnancies from which 160 perinatal samples were obtained.
finding: Cesarean section-derived amniotic fluid was found to be the most practical, sterile, and processing-efficient perinatal source for GMP-adapted MSC-like cell banking.
mod_finding: Samples collected via cesarean section demonstrated significantly lower rates of blood contamination and bacterial contamination compared with those from vaginal deliveries.
